page.layout: One page of text, single column. Running head with page number at top. Below the running text, a heading "CONCIO XLIIII" with the reference "Matth. 19.", then the opening paragraph with a woodcut initial at its left.

main_text.p: unam tantum perpessus fuerit: sed persisten-dum est vsque ad finem, donec cursum con-summauerimus. Sit igitur hæc assidua pio-rum meditatio, vbi pluribus ærumnis per-functi fuerint, ad nouas ferendas se parare, nec vnquam fatigentur, etiamsi quotidiana fit-crux illorum. Et hoc est, quod Dominus Ie-sus dixit, Matth. 10. Qui perseuerauerit vsq; in finem, hic saluus erit. Graue quidem, quo-tidie premi cruce: graue quoque habere vxo-rem rixosam, quæ instar perfluentis stillici-dij est: sed si cogites etiam Christū Dominū tulisse crucem suam, & quotidie multa ferre à sponsa sua: item si vitæ sequentis æternita-tem, & istius breuitatem & fugacitatem con-sideres, leue erit quod in se graue putatur: idque per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum, cui sit gloria & imperium in omne ævum, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XLIIII
Matth. 19.

p.i: Tacceserunt ad eum Phari-sæi, tentantes eum, & dicen-tes ei: Licet ne homini diuor-tium facere cum vxore sua qualibet ex causa? Qui respondens ait eis: An non legistis, quod qui fecit ab initio masculum & fœminam fecit eos?

page.notes: The woodcut initial at the start of the last paragraph shows a letter that I cannot read with certainty, so it is not transcribed. The hyphen-like mark in "fit-crux" is unclear and may be a stop; I have written it with a hyphen as printed. The signature at the foot ("S s") is partly worn and may read differently. The running head "NVPTIALES" has a decorative first letter that is uncertain. The page number "281" is partly worn.
